method: Independent confirm pass: every listed component judged against the current LaTeX on the recursive input route (body entry, declared annex proof and any further on-route treatment cited in evidence) and against the held source at the cited locators; source items compared are the source's presentation of the same definition, theorem or example, its stated hypotheses, equivalent forms, cases and attached claims. Correctness was not assessed.

components.basis: Worked null conditioning event and almost-sure-but-not-sure event, with no conventional value assigned.

components.gap: Grinstead and Snell Definition 1.4 (p. 28), with the odds discussion on pp. 27-28, defines odds in favour of E as a ratio r : s of which only r/s matters, gives the converse conversion p = r/(r + s) from stated odds, and reads odds as the rate of a bet a person is willing to make (2 to 1 odds giving probability 2/3). The entry defines only the number P(G)/(1 - P(G)) for P(G) < 1. The ratio convention, the general converse conversion and the source's betting reading of odds are not given for this entry, and the route states them nowhere in general (only isolated instances occur in other sources' chapters, such as Carnap's equitable odds of one to five for probability 1/6).

On the route, def:p15-general-independence and def:p15-independent-random-elements give mutual independence of n events and of n random variables and state that the full-product identity alone is not the definition; the source's equivalent complement-choice form of Definition 4.2 is the countable-valued criterion of thm:p15-independent-product-law applied to the indicators, combined with the indicator equivalence of thm:p15-independence-basic item 2, both proved.

source_evidence.locator: remark that pairwise independence does not give mutual independence, p. 141

components.basis: The source's coin example: pairwise but not mutual independence, and C independent of A and of B but not of A intersect B, shown through P(A intersect B | C) = 1/2 differing from P(A intersect B) = 1/4.

components.gap: Grinstead and Snell's counterpart Example 4.17 (p. 147), a test for a rare cancer with prior .001, P(+ | cancer) = .99 and P(- | no cancer) = .95, giving posterior .019 so that 98.1 percent of positive results are false positives, ends with an empirical claim: when a group of second-year medical students was asked this question, over half guessed a probability greater than .5. The source gives the task (this question) and the population (a group of second-year medical students) but no design, sample size or uncertainty. Neither the source example nor this claim is presented on the route; the entry substitutes a stipulated model whose weights it declares are not measured data, and it does not record the source's finding together with its missing design and uncertainty; the empirical treatment of base-rate neglect in Part 19 (Gigerenzer and Hoffrage) does not record this source's claim either.

source_evidence.locator: Example 4.17 (rare condition and test, with the report on medical students), p. 147

components.basis: Stipulated model with all arithmetic shown (posterior 2/13, odds 2/11, base-rate variant 2/3, two-alert value 36/47, copied-report value 2/13); the source example's empirical claim about human judgement is not carried over.

Outcome-sum expectation, indicators and pointwise arithmetic; the source's value-sum form follows from the proved grouping formula, and its absolute-convergence proviso is vacuous for finite models (recorded in def:p15-finite-probability-limits).

components.gap: Durrett's 'Notation for special cases' (pp. 23-24) adopts (a) the integral of f(x) dx for Lebesgue measure on R^d and (b) the integral from a to b of f(x) dx for E = [a, b]. Neither convention is defined on the route, although later route entries write Lebesgue integrals that way (for example m(y) as the integral of f(x, y) dx in thm:p15-conditional-density-formulas, and the dx integrals in the Radon-Nikodym annex). Cases (c) dG and (d) counting-measure sums are supplied elsewhere (def:p15-convolution-law, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral).
